question: GQ-001
subject: the one gate nobody could prove was load-bearing
the_situation: gates-are-load-bearing EXCLUDED evaluate-refresh because a scratch copy has one synthetic commit touching every watched path at once, firing all triggers
what_that_meant: its removal had NEVER been tested — the only gate in the chain with no proof it does anything. An exclusion is a permanent blind spot wearing the costume of a known limitation.
the_fix: evaluate-refresh now detects synthetic history itself and skips with an explicit "SKIPPED, not passed", exactly as audit-asserted-numbers was taught earlier today; the exclusion was then removed
why_self_detection_beats_exclusion: an exclusion list is a thing callers forget — I forgot it this morning and it cost a blocked push; a self-check travels with the gate

result.remaining_exclusion: audit-verify-chain, which detects ANY missing gate and would mask every other result — a sound reason, not a blind spot

a_detail_i_nearly_got_wrong: I pinned cwd: root on the new git call after noticing the neighbouring call does; without it the count would read whatever repo the cwd happened to be
